memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Make an atonement cover of pure gold — two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide. And make two cherubim out of hammered gold at the ends of the cover. Make one cherub on one end and the second cherub on the other; make the cherubim of one piece with the cover, at the two ends." - Exodus 25:17-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
On top of the ark sat a lid of pure gold called the atonement cover — often known as the mercy seat. Think carefully about what this meant. Inside the ark lay the law, the very commandments Israel had broken and would break again. And over that broken law lay a covering of gold where, once a year, blood would be sprinkled for the sins of the people. Mercy sat directly over the law's demands.

What a picture of the gospel this is. The law is real, and our failure to keep it is real. It does not disappear or soften. But God provided a covering — a place where atoning blood came between guilty people and the law that condemned them. God did not ignore the law; He covered it with mercy at the cost of sacrifice.

This is exactly what Christ has done for us. Paul writes that God presented Jesus as the sacrifice of atonement, through faith in His blood (Rom 3:25) — using a word closely connected to this very mercy seat. Every requirement of the law that stood against us was taken up and satisfied at the cross. If you belong to Christ, the law no longer condemns you, because mercy has covered it completely. Rest today under that golden covering.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I live as though the law still condemns me, or as one covered by mercy?
How does the picture of mercy covering the law comfort my heart?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, my failures are real, but Your mercy covers them completely in Christ. Thank You that at the cross the law's demands were satisfied. Let me rest under Your mercy today. Amen.
